# googleworkspace_user_alias (Resource)

An additional email address (alias) for a Google Workspace user. Mail sent to the alias is delivered to the user's mailbox, and the user can sign in with it.

Aliases cannot be changed in place, so changing either attribute removes the alias and adds a new one. Removing an alias stops mail delivery to that address.

-> **Renaming a user adds an alias.** When a user's primary email changes, Workspace keeps the old address as an alias. That alias is not created by this resource, so import it to manage it, or to remove it and free the address.

~> **The address must be free.** An alias cannot be an address that a user or group in the organization still uses, as its primary address or as an alias ([Add or delete an alternate email address](https://support.google.com/a/answer/33327), [Resolve duplicate account conflicts](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/p/duplicate-account-errors)). To move an address from one user or group to this user, remove it there in an earlier apply than the one that adds this alias: Terraform does not order deleting one resource before creating an unrelated one.

Google allows up to 30 aliases per user and notes that alias changes can take up to 24 hours to reach mail delivery ([Add or delete an alternate email address](https://support.google.com/a/answer/33327)). The addresses Google adds on its own, such as those in a domain alias, are not editable and are not managed by this resource.

~> **Requirements:** the service account's domain-wide delegation must include the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user` scope, which the provider requests by default.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "googleworkspace_user" "jdoe" {
  primary_email = "jdoe@example.org"
  given_name    = "Jane"
  family_name   = "Doe"
}

# Mail to jane@ reaches jdoe@'s mailbox. The address may not still be used by
# a user or group, as its primary address or as an alias.
resource "googleworkspace_user_alias" "jane" {
  user_id = googleworkspace_user.jdoe.id
  alias   = "jane@example.org"
}

# Renaming a user keeps the old address as an alias that Workspace adds on
# its own. Import it to keep it in code, or to remove it later:
#   import {
#     to = googleworkspace_user_alias.old_address
#     id = "jdoe@example.org/jane.doe@example.org"
#   }
resource "googleworkspace_user_alias" "old_address" {
  user_id = googleworkspace_user.jdoe.id
  alias   = "jane.doe@example.org"
}

# Find aliases that exist in Workspace but are not managed in code.
data "googleworkspace_users" "all" {}

locals {
  managed_aliases = [
    googleworkspace_user_alias.jane.alias,
    googleworkspace_user_alias.old_address.alias,
  ]
  unmanaged_aliases = flatten([
    for u in data.googleworkspace_users.all.users :
    [for a in u.aliases : a if !contains(local.managed_aliases, a)]
  ])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `alias` (String) The alias email address, in one of the account's domains. It must not be in use by any user or group. Changing this forces a new alias.
- `user_id` (String) Immutable ID of the user, e.g. `googleworkspace_user.example.id`. Changing this forces a new alias.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite ID, `<user_id>/<alias>`. Used for import.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported as "<user_id>/<alias>". The user's email address also works in
# place of its ID and is resolved to the ID on import.
terraform import googleworkspace_user_alias.jane 123456789012345678901/jane@example.org
terraform import googleworkspace_user_alias.old_address jdoe@example.org/jane.doe@example.org
```
